purpose: This medication is used to manage heavy menstrual bleeding caused by uterine fibroids (noncancerous growths in the uterus) in women who have not yet gone through menopause. It helps reduce bleeding so you can feel more comfortable and maintain a better quality of life. It is not a birth control pill and will not prevent pregnancy.
how_it_works: Elagolix works by blocking signals in your brain that tell your body to produce certain hormones, which helps shrink the activity of fibroids and reduce heavy bleeding. Because this can lower your estrogen levels and cause menopause-like symptoms, estradiol and norethisterone (two hormones) are added to the pill to keep your hormone levels balanced and protect your bones and overall health. Think of it as a two-part approach: one part reduces fibroid-related bleeding, and the other part keeps your body feeling normal.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes or night sweats, headaches, mood changes (feeling sad or irritable), nausea, bone loss with long-term use, changes in your menstrual cycle or lighter periods, and difficulty sleeping are among the most commonly reported side effects.
warnings: Do not use this medication if you are pregnant or could become pregnant, as it can harm a baby. It should not be used for more than 24 months because it can weaken your bones over time. It is not safe if you have liver problems, certain hormone-sensitive cancers (like breast or uterine cancer), uncontrolled high blood pressure, or a history of blood clots, heart attack, or stroke. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as drug interactions can occur. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you notice signs of a blood clot, liver problems (yellowing of skin or eyes), or unusual depression.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is two capsules taken by mouth each day — one capsule in the morning (which contains elagolix 300 mg plus estradiol 1 mg and norethisterone 0.5 mg) and one capsule in the evening (which contains only elagolix 300 mg). Try to take them at the same times every day, with or without food. Treatment is typically limited to 24 months.
